title: Can you use credit cards at costco? | CreditDoc
h1: Can You Use Credit Cards at Costco? (And What to Do if You Can't)
meta_description: Yes, you can use credit cards at Costco, but only from the Visa network in-store. Learn why and discover your payment options if you have bad credit.
primary_question: Can you use credit cards at costco?
questions_answered: Can you use credit cards at costco?

sections.heading: The Short Answer: Yes, But Only Visa
sections.content:
So you're at the Costco checkout with a cart full of bulk items, and you pull out your wallet. Can you use your credit card? Yes, you absolutely can. But there’s a big catch you need to know about.

**In its U.S. warehouses, Costco only accepts credit cards from the Visa network.**

This rule applies to everything you buy in the physical store, at the Costco gas station, and at the car wash. If your credit card is a Mastercard, American Express, or Discover, it won't be accepted at the register inside a U.S. Costco warehouse. This can be a frustrating surprise if you're not prepared.

Don't worry, though. This doesn't mean you're out of luck. There are several other ways to pay, and there's even a loophole if you're shopping online. More importantly, if the only card you have isn't a Visa because of a tough credit history, this is a perfect opportunity to explore options that can help you build your credit and expand your choices.

sections.heading: Why the 'Visa-Only' Rule at Costco?
sections.content:
Costco's 'Visa-only' policy isn't an arbitrary rule; it's a calculated business strategy designed to minimize costs and maximize value for its members. The decision is rooted in the complex world of credit card processing fees, often called interchange fees.

Whenever a customer uses a credit card, the merchant pays a fee on that transaction. This fee is split between the bank that issued the card and the payment network (like Visa, Mastercard, etc.) that facilitates the transaction. For a high-volume, low-margin retailer like Costco, these fees can represent one of their largest operating expenses, potentially adding up to a vast sum each year.

To combat this, Costco uses its immense purchasing power and millions of loyal members as a bargaining chip. By directing its massive volume of in-store credit card transactions to a single payment network, it can negotiate a significantly lower processing fee than retailers who accept all networks. This exclusive partnership creates a win-win scenario: the network gets a massive, guaranteed volume of transactions, and Costco saves a fortune in fees. Those savings are then passed on to customers in the form of lower prices on goods, which is the foundation of Costco's entire business model.

Previously, Costco had a long-standing exclusive partnership with American Express. When that agreement concluded, they negotiated a new one with Visa and Citigroup, establishing Visa as the sole accepted credit card network for its U.S. warehouse locations.

sections.heading: What to Do if You Don't Have a Visa Credit Card
sections.content:
Finding out your card won't work at the register is stressful. But you have options. If you don't carry a Visa credit card, here are the other ways you can pay at a Costco warehouse.

### Use a Debit Card
Costco accepts most PIN-based debit cards. Even if your debit card has a Mastercard logo, it will likely work as long as you can enter your PIN. All debit cards with a Visa logo are accepted without issue.

### Pay with Cash or a Check
Good old-fashioned cash is always an option. Costco also accepts personal checks from current members, though you'll need to show a driver's license.

### Use a Costco Shop Card
A Costco Shop Card is essentially a gift card. The clever part is that anyone—member or not—can use one in the store. A member can buy one for you, or you can purchase one for yourself on Costco.com. This is a useful workaround because Costco.com accepts more payment types, which we'll cover next.

### Try Mobile Payments (with a Catch)
Costco warehouses accept mobile payment services like Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay. However, the same core rule applies. The underlying card linked to your mobile wallet **must be a Visa card**. The payment terminal is just a reader; the transaction still has to go through the Visa network. Linking a Mastercard to your Apple Pay won't magically make it work at Costco.

sections.heading: The Online Loophole: Shopping at Costco.com
sections.content:
If you prefer to shop from home or don't have a Visa card, Costco.com is much more flexible. The 'Visa-only' rule does **not** apply to online purchases. 

On Costco.com, you can use:

- Visa
- Mastercard
- Discover Card

This opens up a major workaround. For a shopper whose only credit card is a Mastercard, they can still access Costco's deals by shopping online. They can also use their Mastercard or Discover card on Costco.com to purchase a Costco Shop Card and then use that gift card for in-warehouse shopping.

Why the difference? Online and in-store payment systems are structured differently. Retailers often have separate agreements for e-commerce, and they're willing to accept more card types online to capture the largest possible customer base and compete with other major online retailers like Amazon and Walmart.

sections.heading: Costco and Your Credit Score: What Really Matters
sections.content:
If you're concerned about your credit, it's natural to wonder if a store's restrictive payment policy is a reflection of your personal financial standing. It's important to understand that this is not the case.

**Costco does not check your credit score when you make a purchase.**

The cashier and the payment terminal are completely unaware of your [FICO Score](/glossary/#fico-score) or any other details of your credit report. When you swipe, tap, or insert your card, the system sends an electronic request to your card issuer—the bank that provided your card. This request simply asks two main questions: Is this account legitimate and in good standing? And does it have enough available credit to cover the cost of the transaction? If the answer to both is yes, the purchase is approved. The process is about authorization, not a credit assessment.

The real connection between bad credit and the Costco checkout line is indirect. The challenge isn't *using* a card at the store, but rather *qualifying* for a Visa credit card to begin with. If past financial difficulties have led to denials for traditional unsecured cards, you may find your wallet only contains a Mastercard, Discover card, or no credit card at all. This isn't a dead end; it's a clear indicator that the next step is to build a stronger credit foundation. A secured credit card is an excellent tool for this, as many reputable options are on the Visa network, simultaneously solving the immediate payment issue and setting you on a path to better credit.

sections.heading: The Costco Anywhere Visa® Card: A Goal, Not a Starting Point
sections.content:
You've likely seen advertisements for the official co-branded Costco card, the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi. It’s a popular choice for regular shoppers, offering attractive cash back rewards on gas, dining, travel, and Costco purchases. For a loyal Costco member with strong credit, it can be a valuable tool.

However, this is an unsecured rewards credit card, and like most cards in its category, it is generally reserved for applicants with a good to excellent credit history. While the issuer does not publish a specific minimum score, applying without a solid credit profile is likely to result in a denial. This isn't just a minor setback; an application denial still results in a [hard inquiry](/glossary/#hard-inquiry) on your credit report, which can cause a small, temporary dip in your scores. A pattern of applying for cards you don't qualify for can be a red flag to lenders.

It's healthier to view the Costco Anywhere Visa® as a long-term milestone rather than a starting point. For someone focused on building or rebuilding their credit, the strategy should be different. The immediate priority is to secure a card that you have a high likelihood of being approved for and that reports your payment activity to all three major credit bureaus. Use that starter card responsibly, focusing on consistent on-time payments and low balances. After establishing a positive payment history over time, your credit score will improve, putting you in a much stronger position to successfully apply for premium cards like Costco's.

sections.heading: Build Your Credit to Expand Your Choices
sections.content:
The frustration of being limited in how you can pay is a small symptom of a bigger issue. A low credit score can feel restrictive, affecting everything from your shopping options to your ability to get a good rate on a car loan or mortgage.

The good news is that your credit score is not permanent. You can actively improve it. The most powerful way to start is by establishing a new line of credit and managing it perfectly.

This is where [secured credit cards](/best/best-secured-credit-cards/) come in. They are designed for people building or rebuilding credit. Here’s how they work:

1.  **You provide a refundable security deposit.** The amount you deposit is often flexible.
2.  **Your credit limit is typically equal to your deposit.** This minimizes the risk to the lender.
3.  **You use the card just like a regular credit card.** Make small purchases and pay the bill on time and in full every month.
4.  **The issuer reports your positive payments** to the major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion).

This consistent, positive history is the raw material that builds a higher credit score. Many issuers will even review your account after a period of responsible use and may graduate you to an unsecured card, refunding your deposit. By choosing a secured Visa card, you solve your immediate Costco problem while also taking the most important step toward long-term financial freedom.

faq_schema.question: Does Costco take Mastercard?
faq_schema.answer: Costco's U.S. warehouses do not accept Mastercard credit cards. However, you can use a Mastercard credit card for purchases on Costco.com.

faq_schema.question: Can you use Apple Pay at Costco?
faq_schema.answer: Yes, Costco accepts Apple Pay and other mobile wallets at its warehouses. However, the payment card linked within your Apple Pay account must be a Visa card for the transaction to be approved.

faq_schema.question: What credit score do you need for the Costco credit card?
faq_schema.answer: While there is no official minimum published by the issuer, approval for the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi generally requires a good to excellent credit score. Applicants with a strong history of on-time payments and responsible credit use have the highest chance of success.

faq_schema.question: Can I use my debit card at Costco?
faq_schema.answer: Yes, Costco accepts most debit cards. All Visa-branded debit cards are accepted, and most other PIN-based debit cards will work as well.

faq_schema.question: Does Costco accept Discover cards?
faq_schema.answer: No, Discover cards are not accepted for in-store purchases at Costco warehouses. You can, however, use a Discover card for online purchases at Costco.com.

faq_schema.question: Can I use someone else's credit card at Costco?
faq_schema.answer: No, for security reasons, the name on the credit card must match the name on the Costco membership card. You cannot use a card belonging to a spouse, parent, or friend unless they are present.
